channel.title: Kubai Kevin
channel.description: Practical backend engineering, AI tooling, and developer career advice by Kubai Kevin — a software developer with 10+ years building production systems in fintech and AI.

item.title: Freelance vs full-time: African devs' real tradeoffs
item.description: A structural comparison of freelance contracts and full-time remote jobs for African developers: risk transfer, utilization, tax, IP, and a worked pay comparison.

item.title: Distributed locks: safe only with fencing
item.description: A lease can expire while its holder is still running. Fencing tokens, enforced by the protected resource, are what make a distributed lock safe.

item.title: Virtual threads: what actually changes
item.description: What virtual threads change in a blocking Java service, where the real bottleneck moves, how pinning and thread-locals bite, and how to measure it.

item.title: Structured logging: searchable at scale
item.description: Why free-text logs get slow and expensive at scale, and how a stable schema, shared logger, and value-based retention fix both problems.

item.title: 7 ADR traps that cause stale decisions
item.description: How architecture decision records go stale: template bloat, drifting status fields, hidden storage, broken numbering, missing context, no workflow trigger, no review.

item.title: Model evals: the gaps that let drift slip through
item.description: Aggregate eval scores hide subtle model drift. Learn per-example diffing, slice reporting, pinned baselines, and a minimal CI gate that catches behavior changes.

item.title: Canary rollbacks: automate the decision, not the deploy
item.description: Design canary analysis that compares against a live baseline, guards on sample size, and avoids the false positives that erode trust in automation.

item.title: Open source contributions: the credibility trap
item.description: Why merged pull requests often fail to persuade hiring teams, and how to choose projects and shape contributions that read as engineering judgment.

item.title: Saga pattern: orchestration vs choreography in payments
item.description: How payment sagas coordinate steps, why refunds are not charge reversals, and a decision framework for choosing orchestration or choreography.

item.title: WAF and bot management: what they miss
item.description: WAFs and bot managers filter known-bad requests, not business logic. Map blind spots, tune rules safely, and add application-layer controls.

item.title: FastAPI vs Django vs Flask: API picks for 2026
item.description: Compare FastAPI, Django, and Flask on concurrency, validation, ORM, auth, and operations, with a worked latency example and a 30-minute check.

item.title: Queueing theory for backend capacity
item.description: Why doubling traffic can quadruple tail latency, how to model each constrained resource as a queue, and how to measure utilisation before you hit the cliff.

item.title: Pagination for large datasets: offset vs cursor
item.description: How offset and keyset pagination behave on large datasets, where each fails, and how to ship signed cursors that stay correct under writes.

item.title: k6 vs Locust: traffic models that lie
item.description: Why closed-loop load tests under-report latency, how to build open-loop traffic models in k6 and Locust, and how to read the results without fooling yourself.

item.title: Redis vs Valkey vs Dragonfly: which in-memory store?
item.description: A mechanism-first guide to picking Redis, Valkey or Dragonfly: fork history, single-thread limits, expiry semantics, migration tests and metrics.

item.title: USSD/SMS fallback: the session trap
item.description: Why USSD sessions and SMS receipts mislead fallback designs, and how to make the ledger the source of truth with idempotent state transitions.

item.title: Envelope encryption with cloud KMS: key rotation traps
item.description: How envelope encryption with cloud KMS breaks during key rotation, why wrapped data keys and key IDs must travel with ciphertext, and how to test it.

item.title: Async practices that reduce meeting load
item.description: Seven async practices that replace meetings rather than relocate them, with failure modes, prioritization guidance, and how to measure whether they work.

item.title: Audit trails for AI agents: what breaks first
item.description: Design append-only decision records for AI agents: write-ahead ordering, policy snapshots, idempotency keys, and reconstruction drills that expose gaps.

item.title: PAPSS and mobile money: where integration breaks
item.description: Why cross-border PAPSS and mobile money integrations break: hold-and-resolve state machines, identifier resolution, and pending-set reconciliation.
